references.text: The Lord looks at the heart, not on the outward appearance. In [ref:1 Sam 16:7|1 Samuel 16:7], God tells Samuel that people look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart. This parallels Jesus knowing what was in man – he had divine insight into people's inner lives.
In Solomon's prayer in [ref:1 Kings 8:39|1 Kings 8:39], he says that God alone knows every person's heart. That Jesus knew what was in man shows that he shares this divine attribute.

In [ref:1 Chron 28:9|1 Chronicles 28:9], David says that the Lord searches all hearts and understands every plan and thought. Jesus' knowledge of the human inner self corresponds to this divine omniscience.

[ref:Psa 139:1-4|Psalm 139:1-4] praises God's perfect knowledge of man – he knows thoughts from afar and knows every word before it is spoken. That Jesus knew what was in man reflects this omniscience.

In [ref:Jer 17:10|Jeremiah 17:10], the Lord says that he searches the heart and tests the mind. Jesus' ability to know the human inner self mirrors this divine attribute that Jeremiah ascribes to God.

In [ref:John 1:47-48|John 1:47-48], Jesus shows that he knows Nathanael without having met him, calling him a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit. This is a concrete example of Jesus' supernatural insight into people.
In [ref:John 6:64|John 6:64], Jesus knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him. This confirms his all-knowing knowledge of the human inner self.

In [ref:John 16:30|John 16:30], the disciples confess that Jesus knows all things and does not need anyone to ask him questions. This corresponds directly to the statement that he needed no one's testimony about man.
In [ref:John 21:17|John 21:17], Peter says to Jesus, "Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you." Peter acknowledges Jesus' perfect knowledge of the human heart.
In [ref:Acts 1:24|Acts 1:24], the disciples pray to "the Lord, who knows everyone's hearts" – a prayer that reflects the belief that Jesus (or God) knows the human inner self.
In [ref:Rev 2:23|Revelation 2:23], the risen Christ says that he is the one who searches minds and hearts. This is a direct confirmation of Jesus' divine ability to know the human inner self.
